USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current posture and press the Phase One agreement to a signed, enforceable conclusion without imposing new tariffs. In particular, do not pull the trigger on the pending December 15 consumer-goods tariff (phones, laptops, toys), which would fall on US-designed products, consumers and markets and could collapse the fragile truce — but do not unilaterally roll back existing tariffs either until China's agricultural-purchase and IP commitments are actually delivered and enforceable. Keep negotiating with China pushing for rollbacks; our leverage is strongest now, before signature.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderate, not existential. The US has extracted real concessions — China committing to ~$40-50B of annual agricultural purchases, plus IP and financial/currency steps (timeline 2019-10-11; Politico/Livemint). The economy shows strain but resilience: the Fed cut funds from 2.38% to 1.55% amid slowing industrial production and a 10-yr at 1.73%, yet consumer sentiment recovered to 96.8 and Baa spreads narrowed (country_health). The residual risk is a deal collapse and the Dec 15 consumer-goods tariff, which would hit US-designed products, markets, and could invite Chinese retaliation — a real but manageable ~+0.2 threat. This justifies a hold/negotiate stance rather than escalation: escalation via the Dec 15 round would be largely self-inflicted and risks destroying the most favourable negotiation terrain the US has had all year, while full concession would forfeit leverage before China has performed. So an action_score near zero with negotiate is the disciplined read — hold the cards, finish the deal, and decide any rollback only in exchange for verified delivery.
key_factors: Phase One agreed in principle but not signed; signing delayed past cancelled APEC/Chile summit (Reuters Nov 7)

China pressing for tariff rollback; Trump has not agreed (news10 Nov 9)
US holds leverage: China committed to $40-50B ag purchases + IP/financial/currency concessions
Economy strained but not recessionary: 3 Fed cuts, slowing IP, but sentiment 96.8 and easing credit spreads

US-China trade deal signing could be delayed to December... officials said a deal was more likely than not; fate of Dec 15 tariffs being considered as part of negotiations; China pushing for tariff removal.
Trump: "They'd like to have a rollback... I haven't agreed to anything." December tariff round would largely hit US-designed products assembled abroad.
Fed funds 2.38%->1.55% (3 cuts); 10yr 1.73%; IP trending down; consumer sentiment recovered to 96.8.
